newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAFRICA GOVT PLANS ACTUARIAL OFFICE TO COST POLICY.
newsitem.headline: SAFRICA GOVT PLANS ACTUARIAL OFFICE TO COST POLICY.

text.p: The Department of Finance was considering setting up an actuarial office to properly cost government policies and match them with available resources, Deputy Finance Minister Gill Marcus said.
"What is of concern to us is matching policy with resources," she told a media briefing.
She said the department had held intensive discussions with the government actuary office of the U.K. on how to cost government policies on issues such as health care and welfare.

Marcus and Finance Minister Trevor Manuel said this was linked to other initiatives to improve and reform the budget process, including the establishment of a budget office and a debt management office.
Manuel said a draft policy paper on budget reform was being discussed internally and details of public sector procurement reform should be released later in the week.
Marcus said that wide ranging consultations would be held soon on possible reforms to the state pension system, including the suggested introduction of a "pay as you go" system to reduce the deficit.
